description: Use of Computational Text Analysis Methods (CTAM) - including implicit descriptions
rationale: Study must use algorithms or automated software to analyze text data. This includes explicit mentions of machine learning, NLP, automated content analysis, AND implicit descriptions such as: 'big data approach to text', 'large-scale text analysis', 'algorithmic analysis of social media posts', 'automated processing of documents', or 'computational analysis of digital text'.
examples: INCLUDE: Machine learning for text classification, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, automated content analysis, NLP techniques, dictionary-based analysis, AND studies describing big data approaches, large-scale analysis of social media, algorithmic processing, automated text processing even without explicit computational terms. EXCLUDE: Manual content analysis, purely qualitative text analysis, simple word counts without computational processing.
notes: This is the most important criterion: the study must use some form of computational method to be included.

rationale: Study must measure at least one latent social science construct through CTAM. Constructs can range from abstract to multidimensional concepts.
examples: INCLUDE: Sentiment analysis, ideology measurement, communication style analysis, populism detection | EXCLUDE: Simple frequency counts, basic descriptive statistics

description: Political communication focus - including interdisciplinary applications
rationale: Study must address empirical, theory-driven research questions related to political communication, political behavior, or political phenomena through computational text analysis. This includes traditional political communication AND interdisciplinary studies that apply computational methods to analyze political content, behavior, or processes.
examples: INCLUDE: Analysis of political discourse, media coverage of politics, political social media, political ideology detection, electoral communication, policy debates, political sentiment, government communication, political movements, AND computational studies of political phenomena that may appear in economics, sociology, or other fields but analyze political text/behavior. EXCLUDE: Pure economic analysis without political relevance, entertainment media analysis, non-political social phenomena.
notes: Adopt a broad understanding of political communication, recognizing that general news coverage can also be considered political communication.

rationale: Studies that do not use computational methods for text analysis or rely primarily on manual coding.
examples: EXCLUDE: Manual content analysis, purely qualitative discourse analysis, human coding without computational components

rationale: Studies that do not measure any latent social science constructs or only perform basic text statistics.
examples: EXCLUDE: Word frequency counts only, readability metrics only, simple descriptive text statistics

description: Pure methodological focus without empirical application
rationale: Studies that focus solely on developing or comparing computational methods WITHOUT applying them to analyze social science constructs in political communication. This excludes pure method development but INCLUDES studies that evaluate computational tools by applying them to political text data.
examples: EXCLUDE: Papers only developing new algorithms without application, pure technical comparisons without social science application, method reviews without empirical testing. INCLUDE: Studies comparing sentiment analysis tools by applying them to political text, evaluating NLP methods on political communication data, method validation studies that analyze political content to test tools.

rationale: Studies that apply CTAM outside the field of political communication.
examples: EXCLUDE: Marketing text analysis, literary analysis, general linguistics studies without political focus

description: Pure computational method development without social science application
rationale: Studies that develop computational tools or methods but do not apply them to analyze social science constructs or political communication phenomena. This includes technical papers focused solely on algorithm development, tool creation, or method comparison without substantive social science analysis.
examples: EXCLUDE: Papers developing new NLP algorithms without application, tool development papers without social science use case, pure technical method comparisons, computational linguistics papers without social science focus. INCLUDE: Method papers that demonstrate application to political text analysis or social science constructs
notes: Distinguishes between technical development and applied computational social science

description: Survey studies and computational text analysis distinction
rationale: Large-scale surveys alone do not constitute computational text analysis. Studies must analyze TEXT DATA using computational methods, not just collect survey responses. Survey studies only qualify if they include computational analysis of open-text responses, social media data, or other textual content.
examples: INCLUDE: Surveys that computationally analyze open-text responses, studies combining survey data with computational text analysis of social media. EXCLUDE: Pure survey studies without text analysis, studies that only analyze Likert scales or multiple choice responses
notes: Clarifies that sample size alone does not indicate computational text analysis
